section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through mitzvos, the revelation of the name Havayah is drawn into the world, despite the concealment of the name Elokim, because the purpose of that concealment is to enable this revelation, and when sin disrupts this, teshuvah above mitzvos is needed.
section.t: And behold, this is that through the mitzvos it is possible to draw into the world the revelation of the name Havayah,
even though the coming into being of the world is through the name Elokim which conceals and hides the name Havayah,
it is,
because the intention of the concealment of the name Elokim
(from the outset)
is so that through the Torah and mitzvos the revelation of Havayah will be drawn.
And as it is written,
"God made man upright,"
that the intention in the coming into being from the name Elokim
(God made)
is that man, through the fulfillment of the mitzvos, will draw to be upright, "they will see His face,"
that below there will be the revelation as above.
And when they sought many accounts
(the opposite of the intention of creation),
behold, in order that the revelation of the name Havayah be drawn in man and through him in the world,
the drawing must be from the Anochi that is above Havayah,
for this drawing is through teshuvah which is above the mitzvos.
And as it is written,
"Return, O Israel, unto Havayah your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
that in order for there to be "Havayah your God" after you have stumbled in your iniquity, the fulfillment of mitzvos from now on is not sufficient, and "Return, O Israel" is needed.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the four responses to the question of atonement for the sinful soul—from Wisdom, Prophecy, Torah, and the Holy One, Blessed be He—explaining the levels each represents and the distinctions between them.
section.t: D)
And the explanation of the matter in more detail will be understood by prefacing what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said:
They asked Wisdom, "With what is the sinful soul atoned?"
And it said, "The soul
that sins, it shall die."
They asked Prophecy, and it said, "Sinners
evil shall pursue."
They asked the Torah, and it said, "Let him bring a guilt-offering and it will atone for him."
They asked the Holy One, blessed be He, and He said, "Let him do teshuvah and it will atone for him."
This is that which is written,
"Good and upright is Havayah, therefore He instructs sinners in the way."
And it can be said,
that this that Wisdom said that through death there will be atonement for the sinful soul is because even Wisdom is above the light that is enclothed in the world.
For from the perspective of the light that is enclothed in the world,
since sin is the opposite of the intention of the creation of the world,
it is impossible for there to be atonement for this,
and this that from the perspective of Wisdom there is atonement for the sinful soul is because Wisdom is above the world.
[For although the intention of Wisdom here is lower Wisdom,
the Wisdom that is in Malchus,
nevertheless, even the Wisdom that is in Malchus is above Malchus itself.]
But from the perspective of Wisdom,
the atonement is through death,
the separation of the soul from the body.
[And it can be said,
that it is measure for measure.
For the matter of the mitzvos is to draw Havayah into Elokim,
for Elokim is the root of the vessels which are analogous to the body, and the light of Havayah that is drawn into them is analogous to the life of the soul that animates the body.
And since through sins he caused that the revelation of Havayah not be drawn into Elokim,
therefore his punishment
(through which is his atonement)
is the separation of the soul from the body,
measure for measure].
And from the perspective of Prophecy, which is in Netzach and Hod
(above lower Wisdom),
the sinful soul is atoned also through sufferings.
And the innovation in the answer of the Torah, and all the more so in the answer of the Holy One, blessed be He,
is that the atonement is through a sacrifice and teshuvah,
and there is no need for sufferings.
And the distinction between the answer of the Torah and the answer of the Holy One, blessed be He,
even though also the answer of the Torah, "Let him bring a guilt-offering and it will atone for him," is the matter of teshuvah
(for only then does the sacrifice atone),
the Tzemach Tzedek explains in the aforementioned maamar,
that from the perspective of the Torah,
the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
through teshuvah the intentional sins become
(only)
like unintentional sins
(and through the sacrifice this unintentional sin is atoned),
and from the perspective of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who is above Torah,
through teshuvah the intentional sins are atoned,
and furthermore,
they are transformed into merits.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the power of teshuvah from the Torah only turns intentional sins into unintentional ones because the Ein Sof within Torah is measured, whereas the answer of the Holy One, blessed be He, draws Ein Sof as It is in Its essence, above limitation, thereby atoning and transforming sins into merits.
section.t: And according to what was brought above
(section 3)
that teshuvah is in the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent,
it can be said,
that the reason for this, that also from the perspective of the Torah teshuvah is effective
(that intentional sins become like unintentional sins),
even though Torah is in Chochmah
(the chain of descent),
is,
because in Chochmah dwells Ein Sof that is above Chochmah,
and likewise regarding the Torah as it is drawn into the emotions of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes,
that the Torah is in Tiferes,
the central line,
and Tiferes ascends to the Kesser.
But the light that is above the chain of descent that is in the Torah,
since it is drawn into the chain of descent
(in Chochmah and in Tiferes)
it is in measure and limitation.
Therefore the power in teshuvah from the perspective of the Ein Sof that is in the Torah is only that they become like unintentional sins.
And the answer of the Holy One, blessed be He, is the drawing of the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent as it is in His essence
(which is above being drawn into the chain of descent),
for this drawing is above measure and limitation.
Therefore, through the teshuvah that is from the perspective of the answer of the Holy One, blessed be He, the intentional sins are atoned
(and not only do they become like unintentional sins),
and furthermore, they are transformed into merits.
